Christian Horner and Geri Halliwell Buy £52m Historic Estate After Red Bull Exit
sum: Former Red Bull Formula 1 team principal Christian Horner and his wife, former Spice Girl Geri Halliwell-Horner, have reportedly bought Edgcote House, a historic estate in Northamptonshire, in a deal said to be worth £52 million.

The couple are reported to have moved into the property last week, after outbidding a rival bidder for the 1,700-acre estate, according to the Daily Mail. They previously lived at Glebe House, a property in Oxfordshire reported to be worth £9 million. Their combined wealth has been estimated at £115 million.

Edgcote House is a Grade I-listed country home with more than 25,000 square feet of living space and eight bedrooms. The estate also includes two professional racing yards, gallops, paddocks and a private racecourse.

The property has a connection to both British history and television. It was used as Netherfield in the BBC’s 1995 adaptation of Pride and Prejudice, starring Colin Firth as Mr Darcy and Jennifer Ehle as Elizabeth Bennet. The house was also once granted to Anne of Cleves as part of her divorce settlement from Henry VIII.

Horner, 53, left Red Bull in July 2025 and was reportedly paid a severance package worth around £80 million. He has since spoken of wanting to return to Formula 1 and has been linked with the team principal role at Ferrari.

In an interview with The Times, Horner described Ferrari as “the dream”. He later said in an interview with The Guardian that his remarks had been taken out of context, while describing Ferrari as Formula 1’s “biggest brand” and “most historic team”.

Horner also said that any future move in the sport would involve an ownership stake. “I’ve accumulated some phenomenal capital behind me, to look at the next move I potentially make in the sport,” he said. “That would be with ownership attached to it and Ferrari aren’t going to sell shares.”

items.t: Ferrari tension and Verstappen-Russell rivalry shape F1's Middle East return in Qatar
sum: Formula 1 is back in the Middle East to end a season disrupted by the Iran war, but the talk of the paddock is all about personal rivalries, not global politics.
Ferrari is trying to keep a lid on the simmering tension between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after their latest collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix last week.

At Mercedes, George Russell needs to bounce back from another bruising weekend as his old rival Max Verstappen gloated over the “honestly fantastic” sight of watching Russell make a mistake which dropped him to ninth.
After calling off the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian races earlier this year, it seemed doubtful F1 would be back in the region for the foreseeable future.

F1 moved the Bahrain race 3,750 miles (6,000 kilometers) east to Malaysia, canceled Saudi Arabia entirely and started making backup plans to replace Qatar and the Abu Dhabi season finale with a race at Imola in Italy.

F1 missed its own mid-September deadline to decide and didn't make a final call to abandon its Imola safety net until this month, as the security situation remained uneasy but without direct attacks on Qatar or the United Arab Emirates in recent weeks.
The wait-and-see approach seems to have paid off, at least in commercial terms, for two of the most lucrative races on the schedule. There hasn't been coordinated opposition from the drivers, either.

items.t: Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale Drops Hybrid, Gets 670hp
sum: Ferrari unveiled the road-legal 296 Challenge Stradale at the 2026 Finali Mondiali in Barcelona. The non-hybrid V6 makes 670hp, weighs 140kg less than the 296 GTB and revives a name last used on the 360 CS in 2003.

Ferrari has unveiled the 296 Challenge Stradale, a road-legal car built around track performance, at the 2026 Ferrari Finali Mondiali in Barcelona, Spain. Ferrari's 296 Challenge Stradale drops the hybrid system and makes 670hp. It brings back a name last used on the 360 CS in 2003.
It debuted alongside the 296 Challenge Evo, a race car for Ferrari's one-make Challenge series.
The car uses a 3.0-litre, 120-degree twin-turbo V6 with no hybrid assistance. It makes 670hp at 8,000rpm and 740Nm of torque at 6,250rpm. An 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox sends power to the wheels.
Removing the hybrid system helps cut claimed dry weight to 1,330kg, which is 140kg less than the 296 GTB. Ferrari claims 0-100kph in 2.8 seconds and 0-200kph in 7.9 seconds. Top speed is over 300kph.
Ferrari also claims a lap time of 1 minute 18.5 seconds at its Fiorano test track.

The car has a fixed rear wing, a redesigned front splitter, extra aerodynamic elements and a fully enclosed underbody. Ferrari says it generates 617kg of downforce at 250kph, 72 percent more than the 296 GTB.

Leclerc ‘embarrassed’ by Ferrari fallout after Hamilton clash
sum: Charles Leclerc has admitted feeling embarrassed on behalf of Ferrari after another clash with Lewis Hamilton turned the Scuderia's Las Vegas Grand Prix into an uncomfortable spectacle, prompting an angry intervention from team principal Fred Vasseur and a costly 10-second penalty.
Barely three weeks after Ferrari's drivers undermined their team's chances in Mexico through another on-track confrontation, the pair were at it again under the neon lights of Sin City.

This time, Leclerc attempted to pass Hamilton but made contact, spinning the seven-time world champion and triggering another round of awkward questions about Ferrari's ability to keep its two drivers under control.
The stewards held Leclerc responsible, handing him a 10-second time penalty that dropped him from sixth to 10th in the final classification.
Vasseur, meanwhile, had already made clear he wanted a word, instructing his driver over team radio: "Charles, I want to see you just after the race, before everything."
Speaking after the race, Leclerc acknowledged the stewards' decision, although his response hardly suggested wholehearted agreement with their assessment.
"I've been penalised, so as a result, I guess, the majority of the stewards thought that it was my mistake, which I'll accept," Leclerc said.

sum: Lewis Hamilton insists he has not given a thought to signing a fresh Formula 1 deal with Ferrari.
The seven-time world champion’s current contract is understood to run until the end of the 2027 season, with Hamilton believed to hold an option to extend for a further year should he wish to do so.
Hamilton, who joined Ferrari in 2025 after completing a blockbuster switch from Mercedes, stressed he is in no rush to thrash out a new contract.
Asked at the Las Vegas Grand Prix whether talks over a new deal could take place during the winter break, Hamilton replied: ”No, I haven't even thought about it.

"I am in the middle of my contract. It [contract discussions] normally happens some time in your last year. I don't know when we will start those talks, but there is no need to speak or think about it now.”
This weekend’s race in Las Vegas will mark Hamilton’s 401st race since he made his F1 debut in 2007 with McLaren.

Rivian Is Growing Nearly Twice as Fast as Ferrari, but Does That Make It a Better Stock to Buy for 2027?
sum: - Ferrari continues to deliver exceptional profitability and brand exclusivity within the ultra-luxury automotive market.
- Rivian is rapidly expanding its production capacity and strengthening its position through massive commercial fleet partnerships.
- Ferrari offers established profitability and strong cash generation, while Rivian presents a higher-risk growth opportunity tied to mass-market electric vehicle adoption.

Revenue growth is often a key consideration when evaluating stocks, but it doesn't always tell the full story. For investors comparing Ferrari (RACE -1.33%) and Rivian Automotive (RIVN -4.32%), the distinction between growth potential and established profitability is particularly important.

Ferrari has built a highly profitable business by deliberately limiting production, preserving brand exclusivity, and commanding premium prices. Rivian, meanwhile, is focused on expanding production, developing more affordable electric vehicles, and capturing a greater share of the commercial fleet market.

While Rivian is growing revenue nearly twice as fast as Ferrari, their contrasting approaches to growth, profitability, and capital investment could have significant implications for shareholder returns heading into 2027.

Ferrari's competitive advantage stems from its ability to command premium prices while deliberately limiting production. By maintaining the exclusivity of its vehicles, Ferrari creates a degree of pricing power that few automotive manufacturers can replicate. The company also generates revenue through sponsorships, merchandise, and brand licensing, extending its business beyond traditional vehicle sales.

Vasseur shares details of crunch Ferrari meeting with Hamilton and Leclerc
sum: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has offered insight into the crunch meeting between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc following their controversial clash at the Mexico City GP, which the former claimed cost him the race win.

On Pole, Hamilton was overtaken off the track by Leclerc at Turn 4 in Mexico, with the move resulting in Max Verstappen taking a further place off the Briton. With Leclerc receiving a five-second penalty, and Hamilton failing to get past his old rival, neither Ferrari driver could seal the win.

After calling for "serious talks"post-Mexico, Hamilton made several comments aimed at Leclerc, questioning the Monegasque's "do or die" mentality and claiming he approaches battles between the pair differently from those with other drivers.
It was not the first time Hamilton called for change at Ferrari, with the 41-year-old suggesting Mercedes-like 'rules of engagement' after the pair clashed at Monza in September.

However, following crunch talks at the most recent race in Sao Paulo, Hamilton told Sky F1 that the two drivers had "squashed it," with Vasseur seemingly taking step back and letting the pair chat and ultimately move on.
Praising Vasseur's role in the meeting, Hamilton also said: "Everything's good. Fred brought us together. Fred was great in the meeting.
"And then he just left me and Charles to just give our points. We both had a really good, open discussion. And it's all good now. We'll just move on."

sum: Ferrari reported stronger third-quarter profitability on November 3 and raised its 2026 outlook again. The company said higher personalizations and a richer sports-car mix offset lower deliveries during a planned model changeover. The Ferrari results release covers preliminary unaudited figures for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Ferrari generated 1.896 billion euros in third-quarter revenue, an increase of 7 percent from the year-earlier period and 10 percent at constant currency. Cars and spare parts revenue also rose 7 percent to 1.586 billion euros, driven by product mix and customer personalizations.

Operating profit increased 12 percent to 563 million euros, producing a 29.7 percent margin. EBITDA also rose 12 percent to 753 million euros, with the margin at 39.7 percent. Ferrari attributed the improvement mainly to the positive product mix, supported by the F80, and higher personalizations. Higher depreciation and amortization linked to new-model production and increased marketing expenses partly offset those gains.

Net profit reached 431 million euros, compared with 381 million euros in the prior-year quarter. Diluted earnings per share rose to 2.44 euros from 2.14 euros. Industrial free cash flow increased 43 percent to 567 million euros, supported by profitability and working capital.

Deliveries declined to 3,368 vehicles as Ferrari continued its model changeover. The Amalfi, 296 Speciale, 12Cilindri Spider and Purosangue increased deliveries, while the 849 Testarossa and 296 Speciale Aperta continued their ramp-up. Ferrari also said F80 shipments progressed in line with plans.

Ferrari raised its 2026 revenue guidance to approximately 7.65 billion euros from approximately 7.60 billion euros previously. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected to reach at least 3.00 billion euros, compared with at least 2.97 billion euros before. sum: Mercedes CEO and team principal Toto Wolff continues to trust Formula 1 and the FIA to make the right decision about whether it is safe to hold the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix this season.

"Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making. So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that," the Austrian team boss began in Brazil.

This weekend, the MotoGP grid travelled to Qatar. On Thursday, when asked about the situation, Ducati's Marc Marquez said: "I mean, I would like to be in another place. For that reason, I arrived on the latest flight possible, and I will leave on the earliest flight possible. But we are here, we are ready to race, and with full concentration." Moreover, Yamaha is boycotting the weekend completely.

About that situation, Wolff added: "I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that."

The Mercedes team boss continued: "Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

"From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship.

sum: British racing driver Ollie Bearman has had a passion for cars for as long as he can remember. “I fell in love with racing when I was very young, pushing little model cars around the living room. My dad raced at the club level, and I fell in love with it watching him,” he recalls. “After the first time I rode in a go-kart, it was clear that that was my calling and what I wanted to do.”

Bearman stepped behind the wheel at age seven in competitive kart racing, racking up national and continental titles, before graduating to the world of formula racing in his early teens. In 2022, he joined the Ferrari Driver Academy, where he became a reserve driver for Ferrari and Haas’ Formula 1 teams. In 2024, at 18, he made his Formula 1 debut, substituting for Ferrari driver Carlos Sainz Jr. in the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The following year, he joined the Haas F1 Team as a full-time driver, a group he’ll compete with this November during the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

“It’s a cool circuit because it’s a place that I never thought that Formula 1 would be racing at growing up,” says Bearman of the Vegas competition. “There are a lot of drivers who have been asking for a Vegas Grand Prix, and I competed in my first season in Formula 1, so in that sense I consider myself very lucky. I think it’s a crazy, crazy place and a pretty impressive and unique opportunity to race a Formula 1 car down those famous streets.”

As he completes his second full-time season with Formula 1, Bearman continues to be grateful for how far he’s come. “My dad is a big source of inspiration for me. He’s worked incredibly hard to get me to where I am; he funded my career all the way up until Ferrari came along and started helping me out,” he reflects. “He and the rest of my family have made a huge sacrifice to allow me to be in the position I am today.”

sum: Lewis Hamilton is the only driver among the frontrunning teams to have fresh soft tyres instead of new medium tyres heading into the Hungarian Grand Prix.

All four teams also have two new sets of hard tyres at their disposal, making them well placed to follow Pirelli's preferred two-stop strategy: start on the medium tyres before switching to two sets of hards.

sum: While America was celebrating Memorial Day this past Monday, Ferrari was gearing up to upset not just fans of the brand, but shareholders, too. We're sure by now you've heard the Italian brand famous for V8 and V12 supercars launched a new EV called the Luce, and to say the response has been mixed would be blatantly false; the overwhelming public opinion has been negative. Ferrari has even been slandered by Enzo Ferrari's successor. But perhaps the most telling response was that of the stock market, which saw Ferrari shares tank significantly within a day of the new car arriving.

When markets closed in Europe on Monday night, before the Luce's unveiling, Ferrari NV (RACE) stock value was sitting pretty at 309.20 EUR (approx. $360) per share. But when the markets opened at 9AM the next day, Ferrari's stock value had dropped by 6% to 290 EUR. And they kept dropping, reaching 283 EUR when markets opened on Wednesday morning.

Clearly, investors aren't happy, and they're making their stance known. In isolation, the drop looks terrible, and looking at this week's stock value graph (above), things are looking rough for Ferrari. But as with all things, you can't get the full picture from a single snapshot.

Ferrari's year-to-date stock values (below) have been erratic, posting sharp increases and decreases pretty consistently as the markets ebb and flow. This drop might have been significant, but it's far from Ferrari's lowest point this year. On 2 March, stock values dropped to 273.80 EUR. 2026, in general, hasn't been a good year for Ferrari, with prices trading at the lowest they've been, on average, since January 2024.

The stock price drop may seem like a knee-jerk reaction, but it's understandable in many ways, and possibly because of the way Ferrari handled the Luce's unveiling. The automaker had already announced several details ahead of time, like detailing much of the powertrain months ago, and showing off the slick Jony Ive interior ahead of time with plenty of support for its tactile design.

But in Monday's unveiling, Ferrari seemed more obsessed with the design and fact that the Luce could seat five people for the first time in the brand's history. Performance and emotion were almost a footnote in the presentation.

Why Exor's shares still look deeply undervalued
sum: As the owner of Ferrari, Exor controls one of the world's highest-quality luxury assets, yet its shares reflect little of that strength. The investment case rests on three components: asset quality, capital allocation, and the discount to net asset value (NAV).

Ferrari is a high-margin luxury business with gross margins of about 50%. Growth is driven by deliberate supply discipline. Production is constrained to preserve exclusivity, resulting in sustained excess demand and multi-year order backlogs. This underpins both pricing power and earnings visibility.
Returns are driven by changes in underlying asset values, capital allocation decisions, movements in the discount to NAV.
The first two have been delivered historically, although future outcomes remain uncertain.

At about 50%, the current discount is wide in both absolute and historical terms. The opportunity lies in mean reversion. A narrowing towards the historical range implies material upside, even without underlying NAV growth.
The investment case does not rely on strong macro conditions. Instead, returns are driven by portfolio execution and the potential for discount normalisation.
On balance, the odds and probabilities favour a narrowing of the discount.

sum: The Mazda Miata has always been the patron saint of performance for regular folks, a grinning little roadster built on the idea that joy doesn’t need to be expensive or complicated. But every once in a while, somebody comes along and blasts that formula to hell in the best possible way. This time, it’s Rocketeer — the UK-based restomod outfit known for shoving big beef into small, featherweight cars — and its newest creation comes with a stat sheet that feels like it was painstakingly crafted in a spotless shop in Maranello.

Meet the Rocketeer MX-5 Keiryo, a tiny, furious bundle of spritely aluminum whose name literally translates to “lightweight.” That’s fitting, because the company says the Keiryo will pack 370 horsepower and weigh just 850 kilograms (1,873 pounds). If your eyebrows just climbed up your forehead – same. That power-to-weight ratio isn’t merely impressive; it puts this Miata in the same conversation as the Ferrari F40, the Huracán V10, and McLaren’s 620R!

Under the long nose sits a very un-Mazda heart: a highly reworked version of Jaguar’s 3.0-liter AJ30 V-6. It’s a fascinating engine with a family tree that reads like the closing credits of a gearhead blockbuster. Originally a Ford Duratec design, touched by Porsche, then gifted with Cosworth heads — it’s a greatest-hits playlist of automotive engineering.

Rocketeer doesn’t simply drop the engine in and call it a day. Every unit is torn down, rebuilt, fortified, and encouraged to behave as badly as possible (in all the right ways). What the company hasn’t yet shared is how it managed to subtract enough weight from an already light car to hit that 850-kilogram target. The original NA Miata was never a heavyweight, so whatever’s been carved out must be substantial.

Only 10 units of the Keiryo will exist, with the first customer car currently in the works and deliveries planned for next year. If the full Keiryo specification sounds a little too spicy, Rocketeer confirms that a milder “Touring” spec is already spoken for by one particular owner. Pricing is predictably “on application,” which is British for “if you have to ask, it's probably not for you.”

Valtteri Bottas shares heartfelt message to Mercedes as he leaves team for Cadillac
sum: Valtteri Bottas shared a heartfelt message with Mercedes after parting ways with the Brackley outfit.

The Finnish driver had returned to Mercedes for 2025 as a reserve driver after losing his seat at Sauber at the end of 2024. Having previously driven for the squad between 2017 and 2021, Bottas claimed his return felt like reuniting with his family.

After a year out of a full-time seat, Bottas is set to return to the grid in 2026 with Cadillac, alongside former Red Bull driver Sergio Perez, when the American outfit joins the paddock as the 11th team.
The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix marked Bottas's final race weekend with Mercedes. "Thank you, Mercedes," he posted on social media after the weekend came to a close.

"It was great to be back with the family this season during my 'gap year'. This team always has a special place in my heart, and I really appreciate the opportunity to be the 3rd driver for the team. I now respect the team, the sport, and every personnel involved even more than before. Wishing you all the best for the future & see you around soon!"

Mercedes CEO and team principal Toto Wolff gave his full support to Bottas for a return to a full-time seat next year. "It is great to see Valtteri regain his place on the F1 grid for next year," Wolff said at the time of Bottas signing with Cadillac.

"He still has so much to offer as a racing driver and deserves to be lining up in Melbourne for the 2026 season. We will of course be sad to see him go. He has played an important role in our team and his contribution as our third driver this year has been exemplary."

Food hamper on front lawn is 'for anybody,' says Windsor woman
sum: After seeing someone digging through her garbage, one Windsor woman decided to leave out a food hamper

It all started one night when Kaitlyn Ferrari of Windsor, Ont., saw someone going through her outdoor garbage bin. When she went to approach the individual, they took off before Ferrari could ask what they needed.
"I've always had this idea of doing a community food pantry type of thing," said Ferrari, 30.
The next day, Ferrari put several items in a bin on her lawn with a sign that read, "Take what you need, leave what you can."

A Facebook post announcing the pantry idea took off, with Ferrari receiving dozens of daily messages either from people in need, or neighbours who wished to contribute. Every night, Ferrari takes the bin inside to replenish items and to help keep animals away.
Every day, Kaitlyn Ferrari places a bin with food and other amenities free to anyone in need. (Submitted by Kaitlyn Ferrari)

Despite other resources being available throughout the city to those in need, Ferrari believes there are also barriers to options like food banks, such as people not having access to transportation and IDs being required at some locations.
